Grok-4.5 on 04_grid_mingru_sps: official score 0.002
Memory summary

The solution in solution.py implements the three-layer MinGRU policy, grid environment, and full-horizon rollout in CUDA C++ loaded with torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline. Its persistent cooperative kernel fuses policy evaluation, greedy action selection, movement, reward accumulation, and conditional food respawn. The official result was pass, with a score of 0.002 and a clean audit verdict. The score reflects a correct but slow first draft: approximately 292,000 steps/s across all four tested shapes.

Relevant prior context

The agent read the reference implementation, shape sweep, and correctness harness; measured eager reference throughput; checked the reference LCG’s int64 wraparound behavior; and probed cooperative-launch capacity. A probe first failed while requesting a missing GPU property. During implementation, a smoke-test command first failed because torch was not imported, and NVCC then rejected taking the address of data_ptr<float>() temporaries. After removing that invalid launch-argument code, the CUDA extension compiled and a small policy, environment-step, and rollout smoke test completed.

The final rollout kernel assigns one 256-thread block to each environment at a time. Blocks loop over their environments inside each horizon step, with grid-wide barriers before respawn and after clearing the shared hit flag.

Important non-obvious context

The run’s official result records correct: true, failure_reason: "pass", peak_fraction: 0.002, and annotation_verdict: "clean". The catalog also marks it pass and clean. Although the catalog says session_complete: false, the audit explains that Grok’s CLI credentials expired with a 401 after the smoke test. The post-session harness still ran the official correctness check and benchmark successfully.

The audit reports approximately 291.8k–296.5k steps/s across the deck, versus an eager reference floor of about 135.5k steps/s. It attributes the low score to serial per-environment GEMVs: each environment step rereads the full weight set, while many environments are processed serially by each resident block. Two grid-wide synchronizations per step add overhead. The audit contrasts this with a faster sibling approach that batches GRU linear operations across environments and uses CUDA graphs.

The official result lists shapes: []; per-shape throughput comes from the audit’s benchmark log summary. The audit also reports RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell hardware with 188 SMs, and a trace capability value of 8.2. The task brief describes the device as SM120; retain that discrepancy when interpreting the trace’s hardware probe.

Recording summary

The CUDA source defines four real __global__ kernels: policy forward, environment movement, food respawn, and fused cooperative rollout. Each environment’s policy uses the reference gate order and MinGRU update:

const float out = st + d_sigmoid(zg) * (tanhf(zh) - st);
const float p = d_sigmoid(zp);
const float h_new = p * out + (1.f - p) * sh_h[tid];

The rollout clamps positions to [0, 10], uses a first-maximum greedy argmax, and maintains the reference LCG. Respawn matches the reference’s batch-wide RNG behavior: if any environment hits food, RNG advances twice for every environment, while food is written only for environments that hit. The audit verified the gate semantics, LCG constants and masking, tie-breaking, and batch-wide RNG advance.

The audit reports that the official stress-enabled check.py passed for seeds 42, 123, and 456. A separate recomputation probe used novel seeds and batch sizes, repeatedly overwrote the same observation/state buffers, and confirmed policy outputs tracked fresh reference results within 3.6e-6. Environment-step positions, food, rewards, and RNG state were bit-exact; rollout positions and rewards were bit-exact, with final logits within 6.3e-8 and state within 2.0e-7.

The performance limitation is architectural. Each block processes one environment at a time through three serial 256-wide GRU GEMVs and repeatedly loads the weights. The audit estimates roughly 2.37 MB of FP32 weights per environment step, little weight reuse across environments, and up to about 58 serial environments per block at the largest batch. Batching the GRU work across environments would amortize weight reads; profiling and reducing synchronization and launch costs would be the next optimization steps.

Official run effort was 375 agent seconds and 450 total seconds, including 30 seconds of checking and 24 seconds of benchmarking. The audit verdict was clean: framework=cuda_raw, triton_cheat=false, no forbidden DSL hits, and no template mutation. The leaderboard snapshot placed this run 19th of 19 scored cells on the board.
